rules. IUPAC Rules: The international union of pure and applied chemistry (abbreviated as IUPAC) has done a commendable job in framing set rules for naming organic compounds. Two commonly used systenls of nornenclature are described below.
'i. Common or Trivial system (2) IUPAC system [2) IUPAC Nomenclature of Aliphatic Compounds The IUPAC narne of a compound essentially consists of three parts.
(a) Root word (b) Suffix (c) Prefix Root words for alkanes:
The root words for the first four members are taken from their trivial or common names.

Example: for Methane Eth = for Ethane Meth = Prop = for Propane But = for Butane For the higher homologue, root words are derived from the Greek/ Latin number indicating the total number of carbon atoms.
Example: = is derived fro tn penta for five Pent Hex = is derived from hexa for six Hept .= is derived from hepta for seven Oct — is derived from octa for eight
b. Suffix:
